text:
Jack Hughes scored the overtime winner in the Olympic gold medal game in February. Back in New Jersey he's doing the steadier version: 65 shots in 16 games, 8 goals, 21 points, and a team that owns almost 66% of the five-on-five expected goals when he's on the ice. That share is dominant.

If anything, he's been a little unlucky. His 8 goals came from 9.2 expected, and his 12.3% shooting sits just under our estimate of his talent. Nothing in this start is borrowed from the future. Mike Fink of The Hockey News noted he's tied with Arseny Gritsyuk for the Devils' goal lead; our hunch is Hughes pulls away if the shots keep coming at this rate.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 97th percentile for chances from the slot last season, which fits what you're seeing, and two goals against Edmonton on Tuesday were a reminder. The number to keep an eye on is availability: he played 61 games last season, and our projection of about 96 points assumes he plays the rest.
headline: Nothing borrowed from the future
